title: Painting Materials and Surfaces
welcome_lead: Oil, acrylic, watercolour, gouache — choosing material for meaning.
meta_desc: A-Level Art & Design: painting materials, supports, and ground preparation.

concepts.def: Pigment in drying oil — slow drying, allowing blending and glazing.
Pigment in polymer emulsion — fast-drying, water-based, flexible.
Pigment in gum arabic — transparent, water-soluble.
White ground priming a canvas or board for paint adhesion.
Transparent layer over dry paint to modify colour optically.
Thick application of paint retaining the mark of brush or knife.

walkthroughs.body_html: Oil dries by oxidation over days; acrylic by water evaporation in minutes. Oil suits glazing and prolonged blending (used by Titian, Rembrandt); acrylic suits rapid, layered, opaque work (Hockney's pool paintings).

Canvas (cotton, linen), board, paper or panel each accept paint differently. Gesso primes the surface — traditional rabbit-skin gesso for oil, acrylic gesso for either. Absorbency affects sheen and saturation.
Glazing builds depth optically by veiling transparent colour over dry layers. Scumbling drags opaque paint loosely over a darker layer. Impasto (van Gogh, Auerbach) sculpts paint physically.
